situation: Author left academia in 1990 to join industry after failing to find an academic job.
choice: Chose to work in industry instead of pursuing an academic career.
outcome: Income increased substantially and career was established, but feelings of loss persist.
main_reason: Academic jobs were unavailable for their specific field, and industry offered better income.
advice: Focus on making the best of current choices rather than dwelling on past opportunities.
quote: But my teeth hurt when I gritted my teeth and said no. If I didn't have a mortgage then, I would been severely tempted go back to fresh-caught prof wages.
author: Dan

situation: The author felt pressure in academia that leaving implied failure.
choice: The author left academia to pursue other intellectual pursuits.
outcome: The author is much happier and freer to write and learn.
main_reason: The author was not fulfilled in their academic position.
advice: Academic jobs are just jobs, so look for a different job if unfulfilled.
quote: I left academia 8 years ago and am much happier and (ironically) freer to pursue various intellectual pursuits, such as writing and learning about different things.
author: Kaushik Ghose

situation: Unhappy PhD student with poor supervision after four years.
choice: Quit PhD to join a leading researcher at a new institution.
outcome: Lost three years, was underpaid, and realized research quality was similar.
main_reason: Emotional decision due to dissatisfaction with supervision and environment.
advice: Finish the current PhD before seeking new opportunities.
quote: I regret making that decision, because I was too emotional at the moment that I accepted the offer. What I lost in this transition was 3 good years of my life
author: Zalit Forn

situation: Author finished a master's degree and considered pursuing a Ph.D. for a research career.
choice: Author decided to leave academia and enter industry instead of starting a Ph.D. program.
outcome: Author is very happy in industry and avoids the stress of a demanding doctoral program.
main_reason: Author did not want a research career and valued personal happiness over academic prestige.
advice: Evaluate your true motivations for a Ph.D. and ensure you genuinely want a research career.
quote: I am very happy now and can't imagine how stressed out and miserable I would be if I were forcing myself to go through years of a Ph.D.
author: Kevin

situation: Author was in a PhD program approaching their 30s with financial and family pressures.
choice: Left the PhD program and entered the job market with a Master's degree.
outcome: Secured a great job, achieved a happy marriage, and is buying a house.
main_reason: Prioritized family future and financial stability over academic pride.
advice: Consider if pride is worth your family's future before continuing a long program.
quote: I've got a happy marriage, a great job, and I'm buying a house within the next two years, so.
author: Umbrella_Programmer

situation: Student struggled with serious health issues affecting PhD progress and feared negative perception.
choice: Left the PhD program after two years instead of discussing health problems with the advisor.
outcome: Received an M.S. last year with disability services help, but deeply regrets leaving the PhD program.
main_reason: Fear of how the advisor and department would perceive the health issues and affect career.
advice: Open a dialogue with students and encourage them to seek assistance from disability services offices.
quote: Personally, I left my PhD program after two years rather than discuss my ongoing health problems with my advisor. I deeply regret that decision.
author: IndigoJNight

situation: The author was underpaid and their employer refused a salary review.
choice: The author accepted a counteroffer to stay after initially handing in their notice.
outcome: The promised pay review never happened, and the workplace culture became toxic.
main_reason: The employer guilt-tripped the author into staying with false promises.
advice: Make counteroffers official and treat resignation as final to avoid repetition.
quote: Regrettably, I stayed. The pay review never happened. I just got further promises that went unfulfilled.
author: flexi

situation: The author was offered a promotion with a promised salary increase that was later denied by the employer.
choice: The author resigned immediately after the employer refused to honor the salary agreement.
outcome: The author secured a much more lucrative role almost immediately after leaving.
main_reason: The author viewed the denial of the promised salary as a major breach of trust.
advice: Decide whether money or experience is more important before accepting a promotion.
quote: I resigned immediately and ended up securing a much more lucrative role almost immediately.
author: ChrisFNZ

situation: The author was the sole developer on multiple projects, working excessive unpaid hours and suffering from severe anxiety and physical symptoms.
choice: They resigned from their job to escape the toxic work environment and find a healthier workplace.
outcome: They took a break, then joined a startup with reasonable hours and a higher salary.
main_reason: The author was experiencing severe stress, anxiety, and physical health issues due to overwork and lack of support.
advice: Leave the job immediately because the company will not change, and better opportunities with fairer conditions are available elsewhere.
quote: I left, took a couple months to cool down, then walked straight into a small startup company and found myself on sensible 9 - 5 hours and earning about 3k more.
author: Ruadhan2300

situation: The author worked remotely for a company with unreliable and delayed payments.
choice: They quit their job after realizing the owner did not care about employees.
outcome: The company went under one month after they left, affecting other workers.
main_reason: The owner's lack of care and financial instability signaled the company was failing.
advice: Send out resumes and leave the job immediately if payments are unreliable.
quote: I left my job and a month later, the company went under, taking all the other workers with it.
author: Newbie

situation: The author resigned from their job in Toronto to accept a written offer from a UK company.
choice: They quit their current job to start a new position with the UK company.
outcome: The new office was not ready, the start date became indefinite, and the author became unemployed.
main_reason: They accepted a written job offer and resigned from their previous employment.
advice: Stop blaming the company, accept responsibility for the risk, and immediately start a new job search.
quote: The date arrived and the new office was nowhere to be found. The UK company had failed to get their new location going.
author: user7360

situation: The author faced abusive treatment and belittling from a foreman at a new construction job.
choice: They quit the job immediately after two days without giving notice.
outcome: They found a better job within 30 minutes and the boss likely addressed the foreman's behavior.
main_reason: The foreman was abusive, assigned impossible tasks, and belittled the author in front of others.
advice: Sign up with multiple temp agencies to ensure quick employment if you need to leave a toxic environment.
quote: Ironically, less than 30 minutes after I quit, I was on my way to a different job where I was better treated.
author: Taylor

situation: Author was hired by a contractor who lied about their expertise to win a government contract.
choice: Author resigned from the project after the contractor refused to correct the false promise to the client.
outcome: The client appreciated the honesty, pushed back on the contractor, and the author protected their reputation.
main_reason: The contractor insisted on keeping an impossible and unethical promise despite the author's objections.
advice: Prioritize honesty and reputation over short-term gains, even if it means leaving a difficult situation.
author: closetnoc

situation: The author was placed on a performance improvement plan by their employer to force a resignation or termination with cause.
choice: They accepted a negotiated settlement and resigned instead of being fired.
outcome: They received a severance payment and secured a new job before their notice period ended.
main_reason: The employer wanted them out and offered a settlement to avoid paying full severance.
advice: Negotiate a settlement if the company is trying to force you out to save on severance costs.
quote: I resigned in exchange for a sum rather less than the severance. I had a new job before the notice was up.
author: DJClayworth
